## Working session summary

The CV website is finished and PR #2 is marked ready for review: https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/pull/2. CI passes on the latest commit and all 28 tests pass locally. It is not live yet: it deploys only after the PR is merged into main.

**Something you should know:** during the data collection, a research helper put your account email (link.assistant.team@proton.me) in the User-Agent header of requests to the crates.io API. It should not have; crates.io asks for contact details in that header, but you never approved sending your email. Nothing was published, but the address may now be in crates.io's request logs. Nothing in the repository depends on it.

**What the site contains:**
- **Biography and headline numbers:** your bio, plus tiles for 132K contributions, 1,460 repositories, about 305 packages and about 2.5M lifetime downloads.
- **Companies:** a chart of your career from 2006 to 2026, followed by a card for each position.
- **Projects:** a diagram of your personal account and your 4 organizations, and featured project cards you can filter by language.
- **Languages and technologies:** contributions per year, repositories per programming language, and technologies grouped into 8 categories.
- **Other sections:** npm, crates.io and NuGet packages; Stack Overflow; Habr articles and talks; education; and 15 social profiles and contacts.
- **Look:** a dark neon style, built without chart libraries. It works on phones and in print.
- **Icons:** the default React icons are replaced with a "K" logo.

**Why the site never deployed before:**
- The workflow file was invalid because of a colon in a step name.
- `package.json` asked for a version of a testing library that doesn't exist.
- The build failed on a missing package (`web-vitals`).
- The deploy step would have deleted the whole `docs` folder, including the case study.

The workflow now tests every PR, and when deploying it keeps `docs/case-studies`.

**Case study:** it is in `docs/case-studies/issue-1/README.md`. It lists every requirement from the issue with the options considered and the one chosen, and compares existing libraries and templates. It also explains the deploy problems above and records where sources conflicted. The raw data and the online research notes with sources are in the `data/` folder next to it.

**Choices you may want to change** (all in `src/data/profile.js`):
- **Location:** shown as "Planet Earth · remote", because sources say Moscow, Goa and Planet Earth.
- **Dates where sources disagree:** Deep.Foundation starts in July 2020 and Abracar ends in August 2022.
- **Discord link:** copied from your profile README, but it uses a username, and Discord profile links normally need a numeric ID, so it may not open.

I found no conference talks or published papers. LinkedIn and VK block automated access, so I couldn't read those profiles.
